WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, U.S. Senators Alex Padilla and Adam Schiff (both D-Calif.), along with several Senate Democratic colleagues,pressed Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) Chair Michael Selig over the agency’s decision to prohibit prediction markets from geofencing, effectively requiring prediction markets to offer contracts in all 50 states and on Tribal lands. In their letter, the Senators noted Selig’s action directly conflicts with active court orders in California, Michigan, Nevada, and Washington and demanded that he reverse it. “Numerous courts have held that sports-related event contracts are not swaps and instead are indistinguishable from sports bets subject to state and tribal gaming laws…. The courts have ordered platforms to cease offering various prediction contracts in Michigan, Nevada, and Washington, and on the land of two California tribes, and imposed geofencing requirements. The Commission now appears to be encouraging prediction markets to offer prohibited contracts in contempt of these court orders during active litigation,” wrote the Senators. “We are particularly troubled that this action came just hours after the Northern District of California issued its latest court order in Blue Lake Rancheria v. Kalshi requiring Kalshi to geofence around the plaintiff’s tribal lands. This interpretation raises concerns that the Commission may be coordinating with platforms currently engaged in litigation and encouraging them to violate state and tribal gaming laws… The Commission must withdraw the interpretation or freeze all efforts to implement until litigation is resolved.” continued the Senators. In addition to Padilla and Schiff, the letter was signed by Senators Catherine Cortez Masto (D-Nev.), Jacky Rosen (D-Nev.), Maria Cantwell (D-Wash.), Patty Murray (D-Wash.), Elissa Slotkin (D-Mich.), Gary Peters (D-Mich.), and Amy Klobuchar (D-Minn.). Padilla has consistently demanded accountability and oversight of prediction markets following public safety and insider trading concerns. In August, Padilla demanded the CFTC rein in prediction market companies’ ability to offer contracts for individuals to bet on wildfires. Padilla also called on prediction markets to immediately end paid relationships with influencers spreading disinformation about elections. In April, the Senate adopted Padilla’s amendment barring Senators from using prediction markets to place bets on the outcomes of real-world events, including federal government actions and elections. Full text of the letter is available here and below: Dear Chairman Selig: We write to express our opposition to the Commodity Futures Trading Commission’s November 5 interpretation ordering Designated Contract Markets (DCMs) to end access criteria that restrict access to certain event contract markets based on prospective traders’ location or residence (e.g., geofencing) within 30 days. Your unilateral decision directly conflicts with active court orders, undermines state and tribal law, and must be reversed. Numerous courts have held that sports-related event contracts are not swaps and instead are indistinguishable from sports bets subject to state and tribal gaming laws. Your novel interpretation of the impartial access requirements effectively requires DCMs to offer improperly regulated gambling products in all fifty states without regard to state and tribal gaming laws and these state and federal court decisions. There is no basis or precedent under 17 CFR 38.151(b)’s impartial access requirements for this interpretation and indeed this argument has been made in several of the active cases—and rejected. The Sixth and Ninth Circuits have ruled that states retain the authority to apply state gaming laws to prediction markets. The Ninth Circuit has also ruled that sports event contracts on Tribal lands constitute unauthorized Class III gaming under the Indian Gaming Regulatory Act in the preliminary-injunction context. The courts have ordered platforms to cease offering various prediction contracts in Michigan, Nevada, and Washington, and on the land of two California tribes, and imposed geofencing requirements. The Commission now appears to be encouraging prediction markets to offer prohibited contracts in contempt of these court orders during active litigation. We are particularly troubled that this action came just hours after the Northern District of California issued its latest court order in Blue Lake Rancheria v. Kalshi requiring Kalshi to geofence around the plaintiff’s tribal lands. This interpretation raises concerns that the Commission may be coordinating with platforms currently engaged in litigation and encouraging them to violate state and tribal gaming laws. The Commission must withdraw the interpretation or freeze all efforts to implement until litigation is resolved. At minimum, the Commission must expressly state that the following do not violate Regulation 38.151(b): geographic restrictions imposed by court order, those adopted to comply with the Indian Gaming Regulatory Act or tribal-state compacts, and those an exchange adopts voluntarily. We further request that the Commission preserve all records and communications relating to the topics addressed in this letter, from January 1, 2025, to the present and continue preserving existing and future materials on an ongoing basis. This preservation hold applies to all relevant records within the Commission’s possession and any person or entity representing or purporting to be acting on its behalf. This includes, but is not limited to, records and communications via email, whether official or personal; mobile devices; encrypted or disappearing messaging applications; social media; calendar entries; meeting notes; and voicemail and text messages. To the extent that the Commission uses any auto-delete functions, it should immediately suspend auto-delete functions and notify persons with control over potentially relevant records of similar preservation obligations. Thank you for your attention to this matter. We look forward to your prompt response by November 23, 2026, including a written confirmation that the Commission is preserving all records related to this Congressional inquiry. Sincerely, ###

WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Senators Alex Padilla, Adam Schiff (both D-Calif.), Ron Wyden, Jeff Merkley (both D-Ore.), Kirsten Gillibrand (D-N.Y.), and Ed Markey (D-Mass.) launched an inquiry into the Trump Administration’s politically motivated campaign against state Medicaid programs, after the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) withheld billions of dollars from Democratic-led states while dismantling the federal infrastructure designed to detect and prevent fraud. In their letter to CMS Administrator Mehmet Oz, the Senators explained that CMS attacks on state Medicaid programs have undermined fraud-prevention infrastructure within the federal government and targeted Democratic-led states. “The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services is running the most aggressive public enforcement campaign against state Medicaid programs in the agency’s history, while accelerating the systematic dismantling of the federal infrastructure Congress funded to prevent Medicaid fraud in the first place,” wrote the Senators . “That is not program integrity. That is political theater layered over a decade of neglect, with states across the country, and in particular, an overwhelming number of Democratic-led states that have become the Trump administration’s targets, left to answer for both.” The letter comes as the Trump Administration has threatened state health programs with severe funding cuts based on flawed data. CMS recently moved to withhold billions in funding from California and Minnesota without providing any evidence of wrongdoing to the states. At the same time, the Department of Health and Human Services Office of Inspector General (HHS OIG) decertified state Medicaid Fraud Control Units (MFCUs) in Hawaii and New York. Public reporting, including an investigation by the Associated Press , revealed that the Administration’s fraud claims against New York relied on a basic math error, while other withholding actions have sparked lawsuits from states like Minnesota. Rather than working with states to fix issues, CMS has replaced on-site reviews and dedicated oversight staff with a public relations “War Room” and artificial intelligence pilots. The letter points out that the Administration is violating federal law by failing to maintain the minimum required funding and staffing levels for the Medicaid Integrity Program, which was created by Congress to help states fight fraud. Padilla has led the fight to expand access to affordable healthcare amid the Trump Administration’s repeated attacks on the Medicare and Medicaid programs. In July, Padilla joined his colleagues in introducing the Medikids Act , which would guarantee healthcare coverage for every child in America. Last year, Padilla joined over 100 lawmakers in introducing the Medicare for All Act to establish healthcare as a basic human right and ensure all Americans, regardless of income or background, receive coverage. Last year, Padilla and Schiff sounded the alarm on the Trump Administration’s dangerous cuts to Medicare and Medicaid and demanded officials refrain from making additional cuts to the programs. Full text of the letter is available here and below: Administrator Oz: The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) is running the most aggressive public enforcement campaign against state Medicaid programs in the agency’s history, while accelerating the systematic dismantling of the federal infrastructure Congress funded to prevent Medicaid fraud in the first place. That is not program integrity. That is political theater layered over a decade of neglect, with states across the country, and in particular, an overwhelming number of Democratic-led states that have become the Trump administration’s targets, left to answer for both. Since you were confirmed as Administrator, you sent all 50 governors letters demanding provider revalidation on a ten-business-day clock. You moved to withhold more than $2 billion annually in federal Medicaid funds from Minnesota without providing the State any details on its alleged noncompliance, and then issued successive deferral actions in February, April, and July 2026 totaling more than $500 million in additional federal Medicaid funds. In successive deferral actions in May, July, and October 2026, you also withheld more than $3.4 billion in federal Medicaid funds tied to California’s In-Home Supportive Services program and personal care services, citing nothing more than California’s growth rate relative to other states, with no specific evidence of wrongdoing. The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Office of Inspector General (HHS OIG) has decertified Hawaii and New York’s Medicaid Fraud Control Units and placed all 53 Medicaid Fraud Control Units (MFCUs) under review. Though most MFCUs are housed within state Attorneys General offices, all serve as the primary mechanism for prosecuting Medicaid provider fraud; consequently, decertifying them in the name of fighting fraud is self-defeating. Moreover, while statutory oversight of MFCUs rests with HHS OIG, the CMS Center for Program Integrity (CPI), whose statutory role is to serve as the federal bridge to state MFCUs so that state Medicaid program integrity units work in partnership with and refer cases to their respective MFCUs, has provided no visible support to states navigating this review. During New York’s decertification, it appears that CPI provided no technical assistance or support to the program integrity unit, leaving state investigators without a functioning federal pathway. Instead, you have launched a Medicaid Fraud “War Room” that your Deputy Administrator publicly calls “what modern program integrity looks like.” Modern program integrity should start with meeting the mandates Congress already wrote into law. Medicaid program integrity has been under-resourced across administrations. That is precisely why Congress established the Medicaid Integrity Program (MIP) in the Deficit Reduction Act of 2005 and imposed a statutory floor of no less than $75 million and no fewer than 100 full-time employees (FTEs) dedicated annually to working collaboratively with states to fight Medicaid provider fraud and abuse. At the same time, Congress enacted mandatory federal technical assistance, on-site state reviews, and analytical support to states. Those obligations are not discretionary, and CMS cannot treat dedicated funding as optional funding or repurpose it at will. The Trump administration and CMS under your leadership are not meeting these binding statutory obligations. Instead, you are hollowing out MIP under the guise of enforcement and compounding institutional failures: The Division of Fraud Research and Detection, the only CMS division dedicated exclusively to Medicaid analytics, which maintained direct data feeds from approximately sixteen states’ Medicaid Management Information Systems (MMIS), was eliminated in the 2015 CPI reorganization. The defining failure of the current era is that these vital tools were never rebuilt, allowing what was once a temporary reorganization to harden into a permanent blind spot. Comprehensive on-site State Program Integrity Reviews have been replaced with remote “Focused Reviews” issuing non-binding “Observations.” CMS no longer tells states what to fix; it tells states what to consider. Until this administration, even as the MIP infrastructure weakened, CMS and states maintained a working collaborative relationship on program integrity – sharing data, issuing joint fraud alerts with HHS OIG, and working through disallowances backed by evidence. That collaborative posture has been replaced by performative enforcement. The Medicaid Integrity Institute’s residential training at the Department of Justice’s (DOJ) Ernest F. Hollings National Advocacy Center (NAC), CMS’s flagship in-person training for state program integrity staff, has been eliminated in favor of an all-virtual calendar. State program integrity directors have asked, in every available forum, for the in-person peer-led instruction to return, and CMS has refused. Public reporting and CMS’s own training calendars indicate the Institute has been reduced to a handful of virtual webinars per year and a few regional in-person listening sessions with State Medicaid Agencies and MFCUs between July and November 2026. Publicly reported accounts indicate the federal workforce dedicated exclusively to Medicaid program integrity has fallen dramatically below the 100-FTE floor Congress set. CMS state liaisons, fraud alerts issued jointly with HHS OIG, State Medicaid Director letters on program integrity, and the Annual Summary Report of Program Integrity Reviews have all been eliminated or discontinued. An enforcement campaign built on gutted infrastructure produces shoddy results. On April 10, 2026, news reports revealed that CMS acknowledged its fraud probe of New York Medicaid rested on a figure that was off by a factor of ten – a basic mathematical error in calculating annual unique beneficiaries that independent analysts traced to a fundamental misunderstanding of how Medicaid data is counted. The administration publicly shared whatever figures served its political purposes, and the resulting mistake was then used to threaten a state. California has faced a separate but equally troubling pattern: CMS has imposed federal payment deferrals that have now accumulated to more than $3.4 billion, with California’s Medicaid director publicly rejecting the validity of CMS’s claims and stating that CMS has provided no evidence supporting the deferrals. Minnesota has gone further and filed suit against CMS, HHS, you, and Secretary Kennedy over the attempted withholding of $243 million in Medicaid payments, alleging that CMS imposed the withholding, without informing the state, despite it asking repeatedly, how it was noncompliant or what corrective steps were required. CMS is putting on theatrics about going after states to “crush fraud” without any legitimate data to back up their claims, all the while starving the federal office Congress created to help states prevent those failures. A fake war room is not a substitute for a Medicaid integrity program that meets its statutory obligations. Contracting Medicaid analytics out to General Dynamics Information Technology (GDIT), the current Trusted Third Party for the Healthcare Fraud Prevention Partnership (HFPP), a multi-payer public-private partnership, is also not in compliance with a statute that requires Medicaid-dedicated federal capacity. On October 15, 2026, your Deputy Administrator announced at an industry conference that CMS is piloting artificial intelligence to flag suspicious Medicaid billing patterns “in near real-time before Medicaid payments are made,” with the stated goal of scaling the pilots into a “national, standardized, continuously improving platform.” CMS does not, however, operate the claims systems that generate the underlying data. In fee-for-service Medicaid, state agencies adjudicate claims; in managed care, Medicaid Managed Care Organizations do. CMS receives Medicaid claims and encounter data on a lag, and the federal pre-payment analytical capacity that could plausibly support such a platform is precisely the capacity CMS dismantled. Congress is entitled to understand what data CMS actually has, how it is obtaining it, and under what legal authority, before any such platform is scaled nationally. Therefore, to assess CPI’s current compliance with Section 1936 of the Social Security Act (the Act) and the fiscal accounting of the MIP appropriation, I request the following documents and information by November 27, 2026: For each fiscal year from FY 2015 through the present, please provide the number of filled federal FTE coded exclusively to the MIP appropriation, reconciled to the 100-FTE statutory floor under Section 1936 of the Act. To the extent the workforce has fallen below the statutory floor in any fiscal year, please provide CMS’s legal justification for its noncompliance. Please provide SF-133 quarterly budget execution reports for the MIP Treasury Account Symbol for FY 2020 through FY 2025, including unobligated balances brought forward each fiscal year. Please identify any MIP-appropriated funds obligated since FY 2015 for Medicare activities, shared CMS overhead, non-Medicaid purposes, or Medicaid beneficiary eligibility verification (as distinct from the statutorily specified provider fraud and abuse purpose), together with CMS’s legal justification for those obligations under the Purpose Statute, the Anti-Deficiency Act, and the Miscellaneous Receipts Act, given that MIP is a mandatory appropriation with a specific statutory purpose. Please provide the methodology for, and actual allocation of, Unified Program Integrity Contractor costs between the MIP appropriation and Medicare appropriations from FY 2020 through the present, with Medicaid-specific deliverables identified for each fiscal year. Please provide, for each fiscal year from FY 2015 through the present, (a) MIP funds obligated to the Medicaid Integrity Institute residential training program housed at the DOJ NAC, including all deobligations and modifications of the CMS-DOJ interagency agreement, (b) actual institute expenditures by fiscal year, with a breakdown of in-person training expenditures, virtual training expenditures, and non-training expenditures (including per-class costs and number of classes offered) and (c) documentation of how funds no longer obligated for in-person training have been reallocated. Please identify any current, planned, or forecasted contract action, modification, or statement of work moving Medicaid Integrity Institute functions, including training logistics, curriculum development, state travel administration, or data analytics, to a contractor, including but not limited to GDIT. For any such action, please provide (a) the proposed and executed contract value compared to historical institute operating costs under the DOJ interagency agreement; (b) the methodology for allocating contractor labor hours and overhead between MIP-funded Medicaid-exclusive activities and HFPP funded multi-payer activities; (c) CMS’s legal analysis under the Purpose Statute, the Anti-Deficiency Act, and the Miscellaneous Receipts Act of using MIP’s Medicaid restricted mandatory appropriation to fund any multi-payer or non-Medicaid-exclusive activity; and (d) the current status of the CY 2027 MII training calendar, including whether its publication is dependent on the execution of any HFPP-related contract action. Please identify the appropriation account, funding source, staffing plan, contractor support, and Medicaid-specific deliverables of the Medicaid Fraud War Room. Please state whether any Fraud War Room resources, including, but not limited to, personnel, contract, or overhead, are drawn from the MIP appropriation, and provide the legal basis for any such allocation. Please also provide the underlying data documentation for the $203 million and 50-provider figures announced on July 28, 2026, and a breakdown of amounts actually recovered versus payments flagged, together with the underlying data documentation for the updated $342 million and 124 notices-of-intent-to-exclude figures referenced in your Deputy Administrator’s October 15, 2026 ADAPT conference presentation, and an explanation reconciling the two sets of public figures. Please describe the artificial intelligence and machine learning pilots referenced by your Deputy Administrator at the ADAPT conference on October 15, 2026, including: (a) the data sources, data flows, and legal authorities under which CMS is obtaining Medicaid claims or encounter data on a pre-payment basis in fee-for-service and managed care Medicaid; (b) the states participating in each pilot and the terms of their participation, including the Indiana-Oracle pilot and the five additional state pilots referenced; (c) the contractor(s) supporting each pilot and the acquisition vehicle(s) under which they were engaged; (d) the appropriation account(s) funding each pilot, including whether any MIP appropriated funds are being used; (e) the privacy, data security, and HIPAA frameworks governing CMS’s collection and use of pre-payment Medicaid claims and encounter data; and (f) the relationship, if any, between the pilots’ data architecture and the direct state MMIS data feeds maintained by the Division of Fraud Research and Detection prior to its elimination. Please explain how the President’s FY 2027 Budget submission treats the MIP appropriation, the Medicaid Integrity Institute, and the Section 1936 workforce, training, and technical assistance mandates, and state CMS’s position on statutory compliance in the current and coming fiscal years. Please provide all internal analyses, contractor deliverables, and data sources supporting (a) the 5 million people with personal care services figure cited in your April 2026 letter to New York Governor Kathy Hochul, (b) the alleged noncompliance related to the withholding action against Minnesota including the analytical and evidentiary basis, (c) all federal payment deferrals imposed against Minnesota, including the analytical and evidentiary basis for each deferral, (d) all federal payment deferrals imposed against California, including the analytical and evidentiary basis for each deferral, and (e) CPI’s role, if any, in supporting the HHS OIG process leading to the decertification of Hawaii and New York’s respective MFCUs. I also request a staff-level briefing within two weeks on CPI’s current compliance with Section 1936 of the Act and the operational and fiscal relationship among the MIP, the Medicaid Fraud War Room, and the Healthcare Fraud Prevention Partnership. Medicaid serves more than 73 million Americans. Program integrity in a program of that scale demands sustained investment, deep expertise, and genuine partnership with states. Congress created and funded the infrastructure to do this work, and the administration and CMS are required by law to carry out those mandates. CMS is not free to redirect the funding, redefine the mission, or replace true program integrity with a flashy, politicized rebrand. Sincerely, ###

Padilla celebrates new galleries at the California Science Center, including the world’s only complete and authentic space shuttle system on display LOS ANGELES, CA — Today, U.S. Senators Alex Padilla (D-Calif.) and Mark Kelly (D-Ariz.) joined astronauts and local leaders to announce the grand opening of the Samuel Oschin Air and Space Center, an expansion of the California Science Center at Exposition Park in Los Angeles. The groundbreaking Air and Space Center is now home to the world’s only complete Space Shuttle system with a flown orbiter, the Endeavour , preserving a remarkable piece of America’s space exploration legacy for visitors to experience. The new facility features more than 100 aerospace artifacts and 100 hands-on exhibits exploring aviation, space exploration, and the science behind human flight. The Senators were joined by project principles and approximately 30 astronauts, including the full six-member crew of the Endeavour’s final mission, which Kelly led. Padilla emphasized the importance of expanding these historic galleries to ensure visitors have the opportunity to learn about space exploration and recognize astronauts’ significant contributions to advancing space innovation. “From Los Angeles to Silicon Valley, California has long been at the forefront of innovation and scientific discovery,” said Senator Padilla . “The opening of the Samuel Oschin Air and Space Center, home to the only complete Space Shuttle system on display anywhere in the world, is an exciting investment in California’s future – not only strengthening our tourism economy, but expanding educational opportunities and giving visitors of all ages the chance to experience the wonders of space exploration up close. Most importantly, this center will inspire imaginations, spark curiosity, and encourage the next generation of scientists, engineers, and explorers to dream bigger than ever before.” “I was fortunate to command Endeavour on its final mission, and I know firsthand what this spacecraft represents: American ingenuity and the determination to do things that once seemed impossible,” said Senator Kelly . “Now, generations of kids will get to look up at Endeavour and be inspired to dream big and do hard things. That’s what makes this display so special.” Padilla has consistently championed space exploration and innovation by introducing legislation and pushing for greater investment in America’s space program. In April, Padilla, Kelly, and Senators Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) and Ben Ray Luján (D-N.M.) led a push for a strong, sustainable future for Mars exploration in the Fiscal Year 2027 Commerce, Justice, Science, and Related Agencies Appropriations bill. Padilla, along with Senators Andy Kim (D-N.J.), Roger Wicker (R-Miss.), and John Cornyn (R-Texas), also introduced the NASA Talent Exchange Program Act which would foster collaboration between NASA and the commercial space industry by creating the Public Private Talent Exchange Program. Last year, Padilla and Senate Commerce Committee Chairman Ted Cruz (R-Texas) introduced the Space Exploration Research Act to promote aeronautical and space research, educate a 21st century space workforce, and enhance U.S. commercial competitiveness in the space and aerospace industries. ###

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Following Veterans Day, U.S. Senators Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), Ranking Member of the Senate Committee on Veterans’ Affairs, and Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), Ranking Member of the Senate Banking Committee, announced the End Veterans Homelessness Act to help address the veteran housing crisis in California and across the country . The legislation would expand veterans’ eligibility for housing vouchers through the Department of Housing and Urban Development-Veterans Affairs Supportive Housing (HUD-VASH) program while reducing casework bottlenecks that prevent veterans from securing housing. On any given night in America, nearly 32,500 veterans — including over 9,300 Californians — experience homelessness. To address this crisis, Congress created the HUD-VASH program to distribute vouchers to veterans, prioritizing those with chronic mental illnesses or substance use disorders. As of July 2026, Congress has funded nearly 116,000 HUD-VASH vouchers, but about 20,900 of these vouchers are not being utilized in part due to strict statutory requirements. The End Veterans Homelessness Act would help veterans access these unused vouchers by enhancing the efficiency of the HUD-VASH program, broadening program eligibility, increasing oversight, and reducing bureaucratic red tape. “Our veterans have made immense sacrifices to defend our nation, and we owe them our unwavering support, including a stable roof over their heads,” said Senator Padilla. “Too many federally funded HUD-VASH vouchers are going unused every year due to red tape and outdated eligibility requirements. The End Veterans Homelessness Act takes a critical step toward expanding access to essential housing support for veterans and honoring their immense service and sacrifice for our country.” “No veteran should go without food or shelter,” said Senator Blumenthal . “Every year, thousands of HUD-VASH vouchers—one of our most successful tools to help end veterans homelessness—go unused. Our commonsense legislation will help ensure more housing vouchers get used and will put more veterans into stable housing.” “Veterans who put their lives on the line to serve our country shouldn’t end up sleeping on the streets. This legislation will cut red tape in the VASH Program to ensure veterans have the assistance and support they need when struggling to find stable, affordable housing,” said Senator Warren . Specifically, the End Veterans Homelessness Act would: Broaden HUD-VASH eligibility to include veterans and their families who are experiencing or at risk of homelessness and veterans who do not require intensive supportive services ( and are currently ineligible for the program ), while preserving priority for chronically homeless veterans and veterans with chronic disabilities; Allow veterans currently receiving housing assistance through other programs to transfer into HUD-VASH, freeing up limited housing subsidies for non-veterans in need; Adopt effective Emergency Housing Voucher program flexibilities and allow public housing authorities to use administrative fees to streamline the process; and Increase transparency and oversight by directing HUD to provide Congress with an annual report on voucher utilization and barriers to access, and by requiring a Government Accountability Office review of HUD-VASH and veteran housing stability across federal programs. California Representatives Mark Takano (D-Calif.-39), Maxine Waters (D-Calif.-43), and Mike Levin (D-Calif.-49) led companion legislation in the House of Representatives. The bill is endorsed by organizations including National Alliance to End Homelessness, National Low Income Housing Coalition, American Legion, National Federation of Federal Employees, and National Coalition of Homeless Veterans. “We thank Senator Padilla and Representative Takano for reintroducing the End Veterans Homelessness Act ,” said Ann Oliva, CEO of the National Alliance to End Homelessness . “Veteran homelessness shows what happens when the nation commits to permanent housing and the services people need to stay housed: it works. Our new preliminary 2026 point-in-time estimate shows continued progress among veterans. HUD-VASH is a big part of that success. This bill would strengthen and expand the program so more veterans can get housed, and it would bring us closer to the goal of ending veteran homelessness for good.” “I want to thank Senator Padilla and Representative Takano for their leadership in introducing the End Veterans Homelessness Act , which would improve and expand the HUD-VASH program to allow more veterans experiencing homelessness to access permanent housing and wraparound services,” said NLIHC President and CEO Renee Willis . “The HUD-VASH program has been a critical tool for addressing and ending homelessness for hundreds of thousands of veterans. Expanding and building upon the success of the program will bring the nation closer to the goal of ending veteran homelessness and serve as a roadmap for how we can ensure everyone has a safe, affordable place to call home.” “All veterans should be able to access the housing supports that are most appropriate for their needs and preferences,” said Kathryn Monet, Chief Executive Officer, National Coalition for Homeless Veterans . “This legislation is necessary to remove barriers to housing for veterans and to allow them to transition between programs when that is the right choice for them.” Padilla has consistently fought to improve veterans’ access to housing and services. In July, the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act became law , which included Padilla’s bipartisan Housing Unhoused Disabled Veterans Act (HUDVA) to ensure that veterans experiencing homelessness and receiving VA disability benefits maintain access to crucial housing support. The HUDVA provision would permanently exclude disability payments received by veterans from annual income for housing assistance eligibility purposes through the HUD-VASH Program. In 2024, Padilla passed a bipartisan amendment into law to increase and streamline veterans’ access to HUD-VASH housing vouchers through the FY24 appropriations package. Last year, Padilla and Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) urged VA Secretary Doug Collins to provide emergency housing and health care for veterans affected by the Los Angeles fires. In May, Padilla announced more than $110 million in federal funding from the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to support updates at Veterans Home in Yountville – which serves the needs of nearly 1,000 veterans and their families. Padilla believes everyone deserves access to affordable and safe housing and recognizes the need to drastically increase the affordable housing stock to address the homelessness crisis facing California and the country, including through his Housing for All Act . This legislation would invest in proven solutions to address affordable housing shortages and provide a historic level of federal funding for existing programs to reduce homelessness and for innovative, locally developed solutions to support vulnerable populations experiencing homelessness. A one-pager on the bill is available here . Full text of the bill is available here . ###

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, U.S. Senators Alex Padilla, Ranking Member of the Senate Judiciary Committee’s Immigration Subcommittee, and Adam Schiff (both D-Calif.), along with U.S. Representatives Juan Vargas (D-Calif.-52), Sara Jacobs (D-Calif.-51), Mike Levin (D-Calif.-49), and Scott Peters (D-Calif.-50), demanded answers from the Trump Administration after an eight-year-old Haitian child who lost Temporary Protected Status was taken into federal custody after complying with a routine immigration check-in in San Diego. In a letter to Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary Markwayne Mullin and Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., the lawmakers expressed serious concerns about the Administration’s harmful immigration agenda. “An ICE officer reportedly invoked the William Wilberforce Trafficking Victims Protection Reauthorization Act of 2008 while taking him into custody, apparently placing the child in restraints and separating him from the person who brought him for his hearing. Video footage appears to show the use of restraints on a child who seemed to pose no threat to those around him, raising serious questions about the handling of this incident,” wrote the lawmakers . “We express concerns about the basis for this action and the harm it may cause a young child who appeared for his required hearing.” The lawmakers demanded DHS provide updated information about the child’s safety and underscored the importance of holding the Administration accountable. “With this letter, we emphasize that the safety and well-being of children and families in San Diego County must remain the highest priority,” the lawmakers continued . “We also request confirmation on the child’s whereabouts, whether his family is aware of his location, and what steps your agencies are taking to ensure he can be reunited with them.” Padilla has led the charge in opposing the Trump Administration’s cruel and indiscriminate mass deportation agenda. Last month, Padilla demanded answers from DHS following reports of increased ICE enforcement activity in Mendota and across California. In September, Padilla called on DHS to end immigration enforcement activity around San Diego County schools and educational institutions. Padilla also urged Mullin to immediately recall ICE officers hired during the 2025 surge period. In August, Padilla called out the Trump Administration’s continued abuses of power and demanded accountability. In June, Padilla sounded the alarm over the significant increase in deaths among detainees in ICE custody since January 2025. Padilla has repeatedly conducted oversight visits to immigration detention facilities and holding centers across California to examine conditions firsthand and demand accountability from federal officials. His visits include facilities in California City , Otay Mesa , San Francisco International Airport , Downtown Los Angeles , Sacramento , and San Diego . Full text of the letter is available here and below: Dear Secretary Mullin and Secretary Kennedy, We write to express deep concerns regarding reports that U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) detained an eight-year-old Haitian child at a scheduled immigration hearing in San Diego, California, on November 5, 2026. An ICE officer reportedly invoked the William Wilberforce Trafficking Victims Protection Reauthorization Act of 2008 while taking him into custody, apparently placing the child in restraints and separating him from the person who brought him for his hearing. Video footage appears to show the use of restraints on a child who seemed to pose no threat to those around him, raising serious questions about the handling of this incident. We express concerns about the basis for this action and the harm it may cause a young child who appeared for his required hearing before the Executive Office for Immigration Review (EOIR). Our September 22, 2026, letter concerning ICE enforcement activity around school and educational institutions addressed the fear and disruption these actions cause in our communities. House Members of the San Diego congressional delegation also wrote to both the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and Department of Education on October 14, 2025, highlighting concerns from twenty-five San Diego County school district superintendents. The superintendents requested DHS to adopt clear consistent enforcement policies and coordination between the departments to keep schools safe places to learn. This reported detention underscores those concerns. Following this third-grade student’s detention, San Diego Unified School District reportedly sent crisis counselors to Fay Elementary School to support his classmates, who expressed fear and distress. The effects of this action extend far beyond one child and his family. With this letter, we emphasize that the safety and well-being of children and families in San Diego County must remain the highest priority. We will continue to monitor this situation closely and expect timely updates on the child’s well-being and your agencies’ response to these concerns. We also request confirmation on the child’s whereabouts, whether his family is aware of his location, and what steps your agencies are taking to ensure he can be reunited with them. We ask that you promptly review this child’s case and give it your full and fair consideration based on its merits, consistent with all applicable laws, rules, and regulations. Please provide our offices with an update regarding your findings from this review by December 1, 2026. Sincerely, ###

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, U.S. Senators Alex Padilla and Adam Schiff (both D-Calif.) introduced legislation to transfer 847 acres of federal land from the Bureau of Land Management (BLM) and the U.S. Forest Service (USFS) into trust for the Barona Band of Mission Indians. Representative Darrell Issa (R-Calif.-48) introduced companion legislation in the House of Representatives. The Barona Band of Mission Indians is a federally recognized Tribe in San Diego County, which was forced out of their first federally established reservation when the City of San Diego bought a portion of the Capitan Grande Reservation from the federal government to build a reservoir. After the reservation was flooded, the Tribe purchased the Barona property to create their current reservation. The Barona Tribe and the Viejas Band of Kumeyaay Indians also share a joint-trust patent to jointly manage the remaining 15,000 acres of the Capitan Grande Reservation surrounding the reservoir. The proposed parcels in the bill are adjacent to the existing 7,500-acre Barona Indian Reservation near Ramona in San Diego County and have deep cultural and historical significance to the Tribe. Adding this land into trust would connect land between the Barona Indian Reservation and the Capitan Grande Reservation. The bill would preserve existing rights-of-way, public recreational access and public trails, emergency access for federal personnel, and existing water rights and service agreements. “The Barona Band of Mission Indians have consistently fought to unify their ancestral home — and it’s past time we restore and reunify their lands to protect and preserve their sacred sites,” said Senator Padilla . “My bill would transfer over 840 acres of federal land to connect the Barona Indian Reservation and the Capitan Grande Reservation and better protect sacred sites, traditional use areas, and cultural resources on ancestral land.” “I am proud to join Senator Padilla in introducing legislation that will restore historical and ancestral land to the Barona Band of Mission Indians who have fought to regain their land after being pushed out,” said Senator Schiff . “This commonsense legislation is a pivotal step in supporting tribal conservation and cultural preservation.” “For generations, our people have been separated from the lands that hold our history, our ceremonies, and our sacred places. Today, that separation begins to end. This legislation is the bridge to Capitan Grande, a land bridge that reconnects Barona with our ancestral home,” said Barona Chairman Raymond Welch . “We are grateful to Senator Alex Padilla, Senator Adam Schiff, and Congressman Darrell Issa for listening to our people and working together across the aisle to make this possible. By placing this land in trust, they have honored our past and strengthened our future.” Padilla is a strong advocate for restoring Tribal ownership of ancestral lands. Last month, the Senate unanimously passed Padilla’s Pit River Land Transfer Act , a bicameral and bipartisan bill to promote Tribal management of over 500 acres of land in California by transferring federal land to the Pit River Tribe. In July, Padilla testified at a Senate Committee on Indian Affairs hearing to advocate for critical water investments for California Tribes. In March, Padilla and Schiff introduced legislation to transfer 860 acres of land from the BLM into trust for the Pechanga Band of Indians. Last year, Padilla and Schiff announced a trio of bipartisan, bicameral bills to promote Tribal management of over 2,000 acres of land in California by transferring federal land to the Yuhaaviatam of San Manuel Nation, the Pit River Tribe, and the Shingle Springs Band of Miwok Indians. In 2024, the Senate passed of a pair of Padilla’s bills to support the restoration of Tribal lands for the Jamul Indian Village and the Lytton Rancheria of California, the first of which became law. Padilla has now delivered more than $100 million for grid projects across California WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Senator Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), a member of the Energy and Natural Resources Committee, announced $69,814,909 in federal funding to help strengthen California’s electric grid infrastructure against extreme weather. The funding through the U.S. Department of Energy will be distributed by the California Energy Commission to communities across the state. “My POWER ON Act is helping communities upgrade their infrastructure to better withstand extreme weather, prevent outages, and protect families from power disruptions,” said Senator Padilla . “That is why I’m continuing to lead the effort to deliver these investments in grid resilience to California, making this nearly $70 million in funding possible. I’ll keep working to ensure California has the resources it needs to build a stronger, more reliable electric grid.” The funding comes through the Grid Resilience Formula Grants to States and Tribes Program at the Department of Energy, which was created by Senator Padilla’s Preventing Outages with Enhanced Resilience and Operations Nationwide (POWER ON) Act. The POWER ON Act was signed into law by President Biden in 2021 as part of the historic Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act , authorizing $5 billion over five years to help prevent blackouts, shutoffs, and utility-caused wildfires and to help states weatherize their electric grids. California has now received nearly $107 million thanks to Padilla’s legislation – resulting in a stronger, more reliable grid and more jobs and workforce opportunities. Padilla has been a consistent and vocal advocate for the need to strengthen our electrical grid. Earlier this year, Padilla introduced legislation that would reauthorize the Grid Resilience and Innovation Partnerships (GRIP) Program through 2031. Last year, Padilla led California lawmakers in denouncing the DOE’s cuts of $7.6 billion in critical grants for energy projects across California and the country. DOE’s list of cuts includes 79 projects and over $3.3 billion in investment across California, with over $2 billion in projects eliminated from Republican-represented districts in California. In 2024, Padilla announced $600 million in federal funding for California to upgrade 100 miles of transmission lines to improve the state’s grid reliability and deliver clean, affordable electricity faster. ###

CALIFORNIA — Today, U.S. Senators Alex Padilla and Adam Schiff (both D-Calif.) announced that six California projects will receive more than $116 million in federal funding through President Biden’s Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA), which Padilla and Schiff voted to pass. The funding, awarded through the Federal Railroad Administration’s Railroad Crossing Elimination (RCE) Program, will improve railroad crossing safety, reduce traffic delays, and strengthen rail infrastructure in Burlingame, Sunnyvale, Richmond, Riverside, San Diego, and Suisun City. “These federal investments will help make California’s railroad crossings safer, reduce traffic delays, and strengthen the transportation infrastructure our communities depend on,” said Senator Padilla. “From eliminating hazardous crossings to planning future safety upgrades, these projects will improve mobility for Californians and support a stronger regional economy thanks to the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law . I’ll keep fighting to ensure our communities get these critical investments and the resources they need to grow and thrive.” “I am proud to help deliver federal funding for critical safety and modernization upgrades for railroad crossings throughout California—made possible by the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law . All Californians deserve to live in communities with robust transportation infrastructure that helps reduce congestion. These federal investments will help ensure the safety of our pedestrians and drivers,” said Senator Schiff. The six California projects selected for funding will advance grade separation projects, feasibility studies, and planning efforts to improve safety and mobility for motorists, pedestrians, cyclists, and rail passengers. Burlingame Broadway Grade Separation Project — $90.42 million : The Peninsula Corridor Joint Powers Board will eliminate an at-grade crossing by constructing an elevated rail structure and lowering the roadway, improving safety and reducing traffic delays. Mary Avenue Grade Separation Project, Sunnyvale — $15.50 million: The City of Sunnyvale will advance final design work for a future grade separation along the Caltrain corridor. Cutting/Carlson At-Grade Crossing Elimination Study, Richmond — $3.36 million: The City of Richmond will plan for a future grade separation at the Cutting Boulevard crossing along the Union Pacific Railroad corridor. Spruce Street Crossing Closure and Grade Separation Project, Riverside — $2.80 million: The City of Riverside will advance planning and project development for a future grade separation along the BNSF corridor. San Diego Regionwide At-Grade Crossing Elimination Study — $2.73 million: The San Diego Association of Governments (SANDAG) will plan for safety improvements, separations, or elimination of 39 grade crossings across the regional rail network. Sunset Avenue Grade Separation Feasibility Study, Suisun City — $2.01 million: The City of Suisun City will evaluate alternatives to separate vehicle, bicycle, and pedestrian traffic from the Union Pacific Railroad corridor. Senator Padilla has been a strong advocate for investing in California’s transportation infrastructure and delivering federal resources to communities across the state. The Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act , also known as the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law , provided advance appropriations for the Railroad Crossing Elimination Program, which funds highway-rail and pathway-rail grade crossing improvements to enhance safety and mobility for people and goods. ###

Full text of the letter is available here and below: Secretary Burgum, On September 18, The Washington Sun reported that the Trump administration is preparing to develop new, privately-owned data centers and related infrastructure on nearly 18,000 acres of public lands for the across six western states, including Oregon, Wyoming, Idaho, Nevada, Utah and Arizona. Recently, the Department of the Interior (DOI) released limited details regarding meetings that you have taken over the last year and a half with wealthy data center developers and investors. The timing of these meetings taking place concurrently with the administration’s efforts to pursue data center development on public lands raises serious questions about your involvement in these deals. The complete lack of transparency regarding these actions compounds our concerns. The numerous risks posed to communities by rapid data center development are well documented. These projects are consuming unprecedented amounts of water, further exacerbating drought conditions in the West, and driving up energy costs for millions of Americans. Effectively privatizing public lands owned by American taxpayers sends a clear message that the Trump administration continues to prioritize the profits of tech CEOs and shareholders over the American people that rely on public lands for hunting, fishing, recreation, and livestock grazing. WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, U.S. Senators Alex Padilla and Adam Schiff (both D-Calif.) urged Department of the Interior (DOI) Secretary Doug Burgum to reverse and restore lost compensation for maintenance and service employees at Yosemite National Park after facing pay reductions of up to $4.00 per hour as a result of a wage-area reclassification. In January 2025, the U.S. Office of Personnel Management (OPM) issued a final rule revising the boundaries of wage areas for Federal Wage System (FWS) employees – employees were moved from the San Jose-San Francisco-Oakland pay locality to the new Fresno-Madera-Hanford wage area, which resulted in significant pay cuts. While 85% of Federal Wage System employees impacted by these changes received raises, Yosemite employees did not receive pay retention and faced immediate loss in compensation. “It is unclear to us why Yosemite employees have been left out in the cold…Yosemite is already experiencing substantial operational strain, staffing losses, and risks of facility closures. Reducing compensation for skilled Federal Wage System employees will further impair the National Park Service’s ability to recruit and retain the workforce necessary to maintain the park’s facilities, protect natural resources, and ensure visitor safety,” wrote the Senators . “Further, the loss of experienced tradespeople with specialized institutional and technical knowledge could further undermine Yosemite’s ability to maintain critical infrastructure and sustain park operations,” continued the Senators . The Senators demanded the DOI provide answers on what steps they are taking to restore lost compensation, how many FWS employees at Yosemite National Park experienced a reduction in pay, why the Yosemite employees who were reclassified under the Fresno pay locality are not eligible for pay retention, and if this issue has been brought to the Federal Prevailing Rate Advisory Committee or OPM. Padilla has fought tirelessly to protect Yosemite and public lands across the nation. Last month, Padilla led a bipartisan group of 153 lawmakers in demanding the DOI abandon its proposed Yosemite land transfer to a Trump donor. In July, Padilla slammed the Trump Administration for eliminating the Yosemite reservation system, pressing DOI officials on their plans to ensure Yosemite’s ability to manage wildfire risk, enhance visitor safety, and conserve natural resources. Padilla also led his California colleagues in condemning the Trump Administration’s attempts to repeal the Roadless Rule, which protects nearly 60 million acres of undeveloped National Forest Service lands. The full text of the letter can be found here and below. Dear Secretary Burgum: We write to share concerns regarding the significant pay cuts experienced by maintenance and service employees at Yosemite National Park and ask that DOI take immediate action to address these pay cuts. On January 21, 2025, the U.S. Office of Personnel Management (OPM) issued a final rule revising the regulatory criteria used to define Federal Wage System wage areas and modifying the boundaries of certain wage areas. This rule was intended to better align Federal Wage System boundaries with General Schedule (GS) locality pay areas and was supposed to better reflect current commuting, employment, and recruitment patterns. The rule took effect in October 2025, and has been implemented in rolling phases, resulting in changes to wage-area designations nationwide. Despite the intent of the rule, we are concerned how the rule has affected the employees responsible for maintaining Yosemite National Park and keeping it safe for the visiting public. Changes affecting Yosemite’s Federal Wage System employees took place in January 2026. Prior to these changes, employees at Yosemite were grouped with the San Jose-San Francisco-Oakland pay locality. The reclassification moved the national park into the new Fresno-Madera-Hanford wage area, resulting in significant pay cuts for the maintenance workers, trail crews, mechanics, and painters employed by the park. Some workers experienced reductions of up to $4 per hour, with higher-wage employees facing even larger cuts. For an employee working 40 hours per week, a $4 per hour reduction amounts to approximately $8,320 in lost annual wages. Unlike other federal employees affected by the rule, Yosemite employees did not receive pay retention from DOI and therefore experienced immediate reductions in their compensation. This is deeply unfair, given that 85 percent of federal employees affected by the new rule received pay increases, while 11 percent received pay retention to protect them from pay cuts. It is unclear to us why Yosemite employees have been left out in the cold. The Fresno wage area does not adequately reflect the cost of living around Yosemite National Park. Many Yosemite employees already commute significant distances to reach the park, and further reductions in compensation risk worsening existing recruitment and retention challenges at the national park. Yosemite is already experiencing substantial operational strain, staffing losses, and risks of facility closures. Reducing compensation for skilled Federal Wage System employees will further impair the National Park Service’s ability to recruit and retain the workforce necessary to maintain the park’s facilities, protect natural resources, and ensure visitor safety. Further, the loss of experienced tradespeople with specialized institutional and technical knowledge could further undermine Yosemite’s ability to maintain critical infrastructure and sustain park operations. In December 2025, a Department spokesperson stated, “We are coordinating with the Office of Human Capital to understand the impacts and to identify options that may help affected employees.” The Department has had months to act, but it appears that DOI has not taken any meaningful action to protect Yosemite’s employees from pay cuts, even though the final rule from OPM noted that “federal agencies have considerable discretionary authority to provide pay and leave flexibilities to address significant recruitment and retention problems.” To understand the impacts to the workers at Yosemite and the steps you are taking to protect them, we request responses to the following no later than November 11, 2026: What actions is the Department of the Interior taking, or considering taking, to restore lost compensation or otherwise make affected Yosemite employees whole? How many Federal Wage System employees at Yosemite National Park experienced a reduction in pay as a result of the January 2026 wage-area reclassification? Please provide the number of employees and their reductions in hourly compensation. Why were the Yosemite employees who were reclassified under the Fresno pay locality not eligible for pay retention? Has DOI or NPS brought this issue to the attention of the Federal Prevailing Rate Advisory Committee or OPM? Thank you for your consideration. Sincerely, ###

DOJ is also relying on the same unreliable data in its ongoing attempt to block counting of 20,000 ballots in California SACRAMENTO, CA – A federal judge in the Northern District of California blocked DHS agents in California, Connecticut, Georgia, Missouri, Nevada, New York, Pennsylvania, Washington and Wisconsin from carrying out most field operations aimed at uncovering President Trump’s baseless claims of widespread voter fraud. The judge’s ruling cited a recent Department of Homeland Security (DHS) whistleblower disclosure received by Senators Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), Ranking Member of the Senate Rules Committee with jurisdiction over federal elections and Ranking Member of the Senate Judiciary Committee’s Immigration Subcommittee, and Majority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y). The court’s ruling found such operations rely upon flawed, rushed information assembled by the agency through suspicious methods, including something called “supplemental magic”, as laid out in the whistleblower disclosure. Known U.S. citizens are being swept up into the initiative, raising concerns about voter intimidation. “Donald Trump has spent a decade peddling the Big Lie and baseless, disproven claims of mass voter fraud. Now, less than two weeks before Election Day, a federal court has blocked an effort that threatened to intimidate voters and sweep up innocent citizens and noncitizens who have not voted. Federal law protects whistleblowers from retaliation, and this latest victory for free and fair elections is possible thanks to the courage of the whistleblower who exposed how DHS is collecting and weaponizing flawed data,” Senator Padilla said. “But we must remain vigilant. Right now, the Trump Administration is trying to throw out votes in California based on information that they know is unreliable. And they’re threatening to expand this effort to other states as they try to protect themselves from accountability at the ballot box. We must continue to counter Trump’s baseless election lies and do everything in our power to ensure that all eligible voters are able to cast their ballots free from the fear or intimidation.” Last week, in a political stunt apparently based on the same flawed data, Trump’s Department of Justice (DOJ) sued California, alleging it had identified more than 20,000 people on their voter rolls who DHS said were “likely noncitizens.” DOJ officials admitted that the data were flawed, and a preliminary review by Los Angeles County found that out of a sample of 200 on the DHS-provided list, “38.9% indicate that they were born in the United States, which is strong evidence of citizenship” and that over 70% had no voting history and that many of the alleged ineligible voters on the DOJ list had never received a ballot. These new findings were not surprising based on the consistent pattern of the Trump Administration touting thousands of supposed ineligible voters on rolls, which then collapse under scrutiny. The federal judge in this case has set a hearing for October 27. The DHS whistleblower made a protected disclosure to the Senators, which was released on September 14, 2026 and alleged: DHS agents are being ordered to violate state laws and access sensitive voter information under false pretenses. Agents assigned to the “Unlawful Voter Initiative” are directed to use personal information from DHS data to lie to access voter information on state voter registration websites, making false attestations that they are a voter or are acting with a voter’s express authorization in order to access sensitive voter data. Leadership is pressuring USCIS personnel to create law enforcement records with information that is likely to be false, which will have serious negative consequences for eligible American voters and other innocent individuals. USCIS headquarters admits that DHS data can conflict with state records and contain both uncertainties and inconsistencies. Yet agency leadership directed officers to create “TECS” federal law enforcement records that relied solely on unreliable DHS-provided voting or registration data, even if officers believe it to be unreliable. Known U.S. citizens are being swept up into the initiative, based on faulty and rushed data that DHS compiled using “supplemental magic.” Naturalized U.S. citizens are being investigated through this initiative without their knowledge or ability to correct erroneous data, with law enforcement records being generated against them. USCIS officers are facing demanding quotas and unrealistic timelines. Agency leadership is requiring five investigations per hour, or 12 minutes each, only further compounding the potential for errors. As Ranking Member of the Senate Rules Committee and California’s former Secretary of State and chief election officer, Padilla has fought relentlessly to protect our elections and strengthen voting rights. Earlier this week, Padilla condemned the DOJ for meddling in California’s elections. Last week, Padilla demanded that DOJ commit to not seize ballots or voting equipment during the midterm elections. Last month, Padilla introduced the Freedom from Intimidation in Elections Act , legislation to protect voters and election workers from intimidation and threats of violence at polling places. Padilla also led the congressional response to the bombshell whistleblower report that DHS agents violated state laws as part of the “Unlawful Voter Initiative” and called for an immediate investigation into the agency’s misconduct, which has likely led to the creation of dubious lists of supposedly ineligible voters. He also urged California’s Attorney General to investigate the effects these actions could have on Californians. Also last month, Padilla convened some of the country’s top labor leaders to discuss how to strengthen our democracy and mobilize against election interference. In August, he led 27 of his Senate colleagues in demanding the Trump Administration stop its illegal voter roll purges before Election Day. Padilla also joined Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.) in launching the first-ever Senate Election Observer Program to protect the 2026 midterms and maintain election integrity nationwide and serves as part of the Senate Democrats’ Election Protection Task Force. This week, Padilla announced that more than 100 Senate Democratic staff have been recruited and trained as official congressional election observers to be deployed to polling sites across nine states. In June, Padilla joined his colleagues in introducing the Protect Our Polls Act to protect the integrity of American elections from federal interference by armed military or federal law enforcement.

Padilla unpacks allegations that the White House, DOJ leadership, and FBI leadership directed unconstitutional investigations into protestors and demands invoking 25 th Amendmen t WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Senator Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), Ranking Member of the Senate Judiciary Immigration Subcommittee, released a video highlighting the Trump Administration’s repeated attacks on free speech, detailing a recent whistleblower disclosure that alleges that the White House illegally directed the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) to open investigations into anti-ICE and CBP protesters in Los Angeles solely for their First Amendment activity. Excerpts from the video are below: PADILLA REACTS TO TRUMP’S LOS ANGELES AND SAN DIEGO IRAN COMMENTS As one of California’s United States senators, I take that seriously because the president’s job is to protect and serve the American people.
